# Black Friday eve: operations continuity when a critical third party goes down

On the eve of Black Friday, a global outage of the productivity suite provider leaves a fashion retailer without email, chat, calendars or shared files for more than a day. The web keeps selling. The committee, chaired by the business, decides what to launch, how to serve and support customers, and which alternatives it had ready or has to improvise.

> TTX-Zone exercise template. Import it from Library → Exercise templates. The readable part below is generated on export; only the data block at the end is imported.

## Objectives

- **OBJ-01** Continuity on prepared alternatives, not improvised ones
- **OBJ-02** Decide the business with numbers
- **OBJ-03** Manage the provider and the third-party chain
- **OBJ-04** The operational exception doesn't become a security exception
- **OBJ-05** Communicate without the usual channel

## Scenario

{organization} is a global fashion group, listed on the stock market, with thousands of stores and an online channel that brings in {online_share} of revenue. Tonight at midnight the {brand} Black Friday campaign goes live: media are booked, stock is in place and the war room is set up. It is Thursday, 18:00. Email, chat, calendars and shared files stop working at the same time, and not only for you: {collab_suite} is down worldwide. The online shop and the payment gateway run elsewhere and still work. Almost everything else you use to coordinate the business does not.

## Phases and injects

### PH-01 Black Friday eve goes dark

Thursday, 18:00. Six hours to the Black Friday launch.

- **INJ-01** (T+3′) Mail, chat, calendar and files won't load
- **INJ-02** (T+14′) The provider confirms a global outage
- **INJ-03** (T+20′) Security tools light up with our own traffic
- **INJ-04** (T+29′) The war room, the plan and the support number live in the suite
- **POL-05** (T+37′) Where does the committee meet?
  - Which channel does the crisis committee use from now on?
    - The pre-agreed alternative channel in the plan
      - If it exists and people know it, the committee is meeting within minutes. If it doesn't, you discover it now: nobody has the access details and the decision moves to option 2, 3 or 4.
    - A group on a personal messaging app
      - Fast and familiar. Decisions, figures and customer data end up on personal phones with no record or control.
    - Personal email accounts
      - Everyone has one, but the company's information leaves its control and the domains can't be verified.
    - Phone conference and in person at head office
      - Reliable and under control, but slower. Someone has to keep the minutes by hand.
- **INJ-06** (T+45′) What does every hour cost?
- **INJ-07** (contingent) The broker calls

### PH-02 Launch Black Friday or not

Thursday, 21:30. The suite comes back and drops again. The launch is at 00:00; the decision, at 23:00.

- **INJ-08** (T+57′) "Restored services may stop responding again"
- **INJ-09** (T+64′) "Media is paid for"
- **INJ-10** (T+72′) Carriers and the call center without a channel
- **POL-11** (T+85′) Black Friday go/no-go
  - What do you do with the Black Friday launch?
    - Full launch at 00:00
      - Sales follow the plan overnight. By morning, thousands of orders have no confirmed pick-up, some products are oversold, and complaints arrive at a call center that can barely cope.
    - Launch without a delivery promise, and with stock caps on key lines
      - You keep most of the night's sales. Delivery dates are honest and conversion drops a few points.
    - Delay the launch by 12 hours
      - Part of tonight's media spend is wasted. Some customers buy from the competitors that are open. You launch in the morning with the stores open.
    - Wait until the provider confirms recovery
      - No orders you can't serve, but no Black Friday either while the outage lasts. Nobody knows how long that will be.
- **DSC-12** (T+94′) The threat the outage brings
- **POL-13** (T+106′) A preventive warning?
  - Who do you warn about the outage-themed fraud, and when?
    - Staff and customers now: SMS, store managers, the website, the app and social media
      - The message ("no support team will ever ask for your code or password") arrives before the calls. Some customers ask whether their data is at risk.
    - Staff only, through store managers and SMS
      - Staff are ready. Customers will find out from the fraudsters.
    - Wait until we see a campaign
      - No noise tonight. If the campaign comes, it will meet people who don't know the rule.
- **INJ-14** (contingent) Sign-in fails, and the emergency accounts are behind the same door

### PH-03 Black Friday without email

Friday, 10:00. Stores open. Chat is back; email is not.

- **INJ-15** (T+118′) Chat comes back, email doesn't
- **INJ-16** (T+125′) Reinforcements with no device
- **POL-17** (T+133′) Do we reinforce other customer service channels?
  - How do you reinforce customer service on Black Friday?
    - Expand the call center: more BPO agents, extended hours and an IVR message about the outage
      - Queues fall below 10 minutes by the afternoon. It costs the BPO premium and the overtime, and the IVR message answers half the calls on its own.
    - Route customers to stores and to the web chat, which doesn't depend on the suite
      - The phone line eases, but stores already stretched by click-and-collect take the overflow.
    - Publish the phone number and a notice on the web, the app and social media, and accept the queues
      - Customers know what's happening and many wait. The queues continue and the BPO's SLA penalties start to run.
    - Don't reinforce; wait for email to return
      - No extra cost today. Unanswered customers turn to social media and some cancel their orders.
- **INJ-18** (T+143′) A supplier changes its bank account by phone
- **INJ-19** (contingent) A regional manager approves a push
- **POL-20** (T+157′) Black Friday trading update promised for Monday
  - What do you do with Monday's trading update?
    - Keep the date with partial figures, stating their limits
      - The market gets the update on time. If the figures change later, you'll have to correct them in public.
    - Postpone it and say so today
      - Analysts read it as a sign of impact. The figures will be complete when they come.
    - Publish only an estimated range
      - It buys time, but it commits you to a range you can't yet verify.
- **INJ-21** (T+168′) Delays, a fake refund text and a journalist

### PH-04 Email comes back

Friday, 18:00. Email is coming back, with huge queues.

- **POL-22** (T+187′) {queued_emails} queued messages
  - How do you release the queue?
    - Release everything now
      - Orders and confirmations flow at once, along with whatever slipped past the degraded filters.
    - Scan everything again before releasing
      - Nothing harmful gets through, but supplier orders arrive a day late, in the middle of the peak.
    - Prioritize supplier and carrier traffic after a quick review, and scan the rest
      - The business restarts in hours and the risk is limited to a known set of senders.
- **INJ-23** (T+196′) "We are deeply sorry"

### PH-05 Saturday: the reckoning

Saturday, 10:00. The provider declares the service fully restored. The board wants figures by Monday.

- **DSC-24** (T+207′) It's the second time
- **DSC-25** (T+215′) The board wants figures by Monday
- **DSC-26** (T+226′) What else hangs from a single provider?

## Simulated actors

- **ACT-01** Productivity suite provider
- **ACT-02** Employee
- **ACT-03** SOC
- **ACT-04** Main carrier
- **ACT-05** Customer service BPO
- **ACT-06** Cyber insurer (broker)
- **ACT-07** Threat intelligence provider
- **ACT-08** Press and financial analysts
- **ACT-09** Customers
- **ACT-10** Board chair

## Placeholders

- `{organization}` The organization the exercise is about.
- `{online_share}` The share of revenue that comes from the online channel, as a phrase. (e.g. about a quarter)
- `{brand}` The retail brand running the Black Friday campaign. (e.g. Kubo)
- `{collab_suite}` The email, chat and shared-files suite that goes down. Written mid-sentence: use a name or a phrase such as the suggested one. (e.g. the productivity suite)
- `{attacker_group}` The name of the group behind the phishing campaign (the threat actor). (e.g. Marea)
- `{online_revenue_hour}` What the online channel sells per hour at tonight's peak. (e.g. €4 million)
- `{media_spend}` Black Friday media already committed that can't be recovered. (e.g. €12 million)
- `{carrier_penalty}` What the carrier charges for missed collection slots. (e.g. €300,000 a day)
- `{staff_count}` How many employees the group has. (e.g. 120,000)
- `{temp_staff}` Temporary Black Friday staff due to start that morning. (e.g. 3,000)
- `{queued_emails}` Messages waiting when email delivery resumes. (e.g. 1.2 million)
- `{lost_sales}` First estimate of what the outage cost. (e.g. over €60 million)

        "content": "The SIEM correlates thousands of failed sign-ins per minute, about thirty times the usual rate, and raises brute-force alerts.
